# dlabad

> Takes the square root of the overflow and underflow thresholds if the.

<section class="intro">

exponent range is very large.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlabad from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlabad';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlabad( small, large ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `small` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): underflow threshold as computed by dlamch |
| `large` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): overflow threshold as computed by dlamch |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `small`: On entry, the underflow threshold as computed by DLAMCH. On exit, the unchanged value `SMALL`.
- `large`: On entry, the overflow threshold as computed by DLAMCH. On exit, the unchanged value `LARGE`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlabad.ndarray( small, large ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `small` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): underflow threshold as computed by dlamch |
| `large` | `Float64Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): overflow threshold as computed by dlamch |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `small`: On entry, the underflow threshold as computed by DLAMCH. On exit, the unchanged value `SMALL`.
- `large`: On entry, the overflow threshold as computed by DLAMCH. On exit, the unchanged value `LARGE`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlabad()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLABAD`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlabad.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlabad from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlabad';

// Using the standard interface:
const small = new Float64Array( 1 );
const large = new Float64Array( 1 );

small[ 0 ] = 1;
large[ 0 ] = 1;
dlabad( small, large );
let out = {
	'small': small[ 0 ],
	'large': large[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
small[ 0 ] = 1;
large[ 0 ] = 1;
dlabad.ndarray( small, large );
out = {
	'small': small[ 0 ],
	'large': large[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLABAD`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLABAD is a no-op and kept for compatibility reasons. It used to correct the overflow/underflow behavior of machines that are not IEEE-754 compliant.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
